gates.blocker: Unblocked 2026-10-11 05:53 UTC. The expired sk_test key found on 2026-10-10 (PaymentReconciliationService logged 'Expired API Key provided ... code: api_key_expired' on every scheduled run) was rotated and the API container recreated with docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --force-recreate app. Verified by production audit row id=87 at 2026-10-11 05:53:48, 'Checked 0 Stripe intents; 0 issue(s)': audit() is only reached after fetchRecentIntents() returns, so the row proves the Stripe call authenticated. Container healthy, Flyway 23 validated, zero reconciliation failures since boot. STRIPE_PAYMENT LEGS NOW VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-11, using the production container's own rotated key against Stripe's TEST API via StripeLifecycleTest (the exact StripeService methods the backend calls): create customer -> SetupIntent -> attach pm_card_visa (read back 4242/visa) -> Express Connect account + onboarding link -> authorize 15000 cad hold (requires_capture) -> capture (succeeded) -> authorize 9000 cad -> release (canceled, never charged). 3 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped. Webhooks verified live too: Stripe delivered payment_intent.succeeded and payment_intent.canceled to https://api.rapidstylers.ca/rapid_stylers/stripe/webhook and the backend signature-verified and processed them, logging 'Stripe webhook no-match: ... no booking for payment intent' (correct: the e2e intents have no local appointment). NEW DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED, NOT YET DEPLOYED: PaymentReconciliationService.fetchRecentIntents() built its lookback with a bare .setCreated(sinceEpoch), which Stripe treats as an EXACT-second match, not a lower bound, so every scheduled run fetched 0 intents and reported '0 issue(s)' while examining nothing. The earlier claim that 'Checked 0 Stripe intents' was expected because the account had no intents in the window is disproven: the account has 52 intents inside 72h, all created before the fix. Fixed to created[gte] with a regression test asserting the range shape; verified live: old params 0 intents, new params 52. Payment package 1218 tests, 0 failures. The fix is LOCAL ONLY - the running VPS container still has the buggy filter until the backend image is rebuilt and redeployed. What remains for this gate: deploy that fix, then refunds, disputes, cancellation through the app, ownership denials, and the dev CI secret scan. OTP and signed-upload legs were verified locally on 2026-10-10 (stylist sign-up used the signup upload pass; upload intercepted before any network egress).
gates.requirement: OTP, signed uploads, Stripe test payments/webhooks/cancellation/refunds and ownership denials pass; dev CI including secret scan passes for the candidate.

gates.blocker: Partial, verified 2026-10-11. Playwright now runs five projects: desktop Chromium, iPhone Chromium, Firefox, WebKit (desktop Safari engine) and iPhone WebKit, all 30/30 passing, 150 tests across 6 maintained spec files, exit 0. The earlier record of 'Chromium 20/20, WebKit 13/17, Firefox could not launch' is superseded: Firefox launches and passes, and the 4 admin-registration WebKit failures plus the iPhone failures were real defects that are now fixed. (1) WebKit refuses to write a Blob or File into IndexedDB - the transaction aborts with 'Error preparing Blob/File data to be stored in object store' - so on Safari and iPhone the professional's photos were silently lost on every reload; photos are now stored as bytes with name and type attached, which every engine accepts, and a unit regression pins the stored shape. (2) The photo namespace was re-decided per storage call, but a document can never re-acquire a lock name it already holds, so the read and the write landed in different databases; the claim is now settled once per document and a probe across a real navigation in both engines proved the stored name is handed back after a reload. (3) The stylist Calendar laid out at 436px inside a 390px viewport - Chromium hides this because its innerWidth expands to the content while WebKit's does not - fixed by letting the month controls wrap; all nine stylist tabs now measure 390px. (4) Specs branched on the project name 'mobile', so the iPhone WebKit project silently skipped every phone-only check; they now branch on the viewport or on what is visible. STILL BLOCKING SIGN-OFF: every run intercepts external traffic with fixtures, so this is engine coverage, not live coverage. Section 3 still requires real installed Safari and Firefox and a physical iPhone against the live site, plus production performance measurements, before the gate can close.
gates.requirement: Supported Safari and Firefox flows are verified in addition to Chromium.
